cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Hi everyone, in this session I'll be presenting my research about the social history of

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Britain during the Industrial Revolution.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I particularly looked at how ordinary lives were affected by changes that happened at

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: that time.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: This was a time that saw the beginning of a new phenomenon; consumerism – where buying

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: and selling goods became a major part of ordinary people's lives.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: In fact, it was in the 19th century that the quantity and quality of people's possessions

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: was used as an indication of the wealth of the country.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Before this, the vast majority of people had very few possessions, but all that was

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: changed by the Industrial Revolution.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: This was the era from the mid-18th to the late 19th century, when improvements in how

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: goods were made as well as in technology triggered massive social changes that

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: transformed life for just about everybody in several key areas.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: First let's look at manufacturing.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: When it comes to manufacturing, we tend to think of the Industrial Revolution in images

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: of steam engines and coal.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: And it's true that the Industrial Revolution couldn't have taken place at all if it

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: weren't for these new sources of power.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: They marked an important shift away from the traditional watermills and windmills that

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: had dominated before this.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: The most advanced industry for much of the 19th century was textiles.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: This meant that fashionable fabrics, and lace and ribbons were made available to everyone.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Before the Industrial Revolution, most people made goods to sell in small workshops,

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: often in their own homes.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But enormous new machines were now being created that could produce the goods faster and

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: on a larger scale, and these required a lot more space.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: So large factories were built, replacing the workshops, and forcing workers to travel to

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: work. In fact, large numbers of people migrated from villages into towns as a result.
